name: Breastplate
overview: The breastplate, crafted with skill and made from gold, fine linen, and precious stones, was an integral part of the high priest's garments, inseparably joined to the ephod as described in Exodus 28. It bore four rows of carefully set stones, each engraved with the names of the tribes of Israel, symbolizing the priest's role in representing the people before God. This breastplate not only served as a physical adornment but also embodied the righteous judgment of Christ, highlighting its significance in both ceremonial function and spiritual symbolism.
